 SPEAK UP: BTS’ Taiwan concerts, Golden Horse Awards to cause sensations (1/2) BTS巡演、金馬獎引爆娛樂高潮（上）
 Add TT as Preferred Source 
 A: It’s been a wild week in the entertainment world, with K-pop sensation BTS finally returning to Taiwan, and the 63rd Golden Horse Awards on the horizon.
 B: BTS is touring Taiwan again after an 8-year hiatus since 2018, holding three concerts at Kaohsiung’s National Stadium on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday.
 A: I even prayed to the Matchmaker God “Yuexia Laoren,” asking him to connect me with BTS through his divine red string, but still couldn’t get any tickets. 
 K-pop supergroup BTS 南韓防彈少年團BTS。
 Photo: Netflix 照片：網飛：
 B: Aren’t Vieshow Cinemas going to live stream the concerts? 
 A: Oh, that’s right. Vieshow is going to show the concerts at 18 cinemas across Taiwan. Let me check online to see if I can still get tickets.
 A: 本週娛樂圈高潮不斷，南韓天團防彈少年團BTS終於來台啦，影壇盛事金馬獎也即將登場。
 B: BTS自2018年後相隔8年再度來台巡演，於本週四、六、日，在高雄國家體育場嗨唱3場！ 
 A: 我還特別去拜「月下老人」請他幫我和BTS 牽線，可惜還是沒搶到門票。
 B: 威秀影城不是將進行演唱會直播嗎？
 A: 哈對耶，威秀在全台18家影城推出同步直播，我趕快上網試試看還能不能搶到票。
 （By Eddy Chang, Taipei Times／台北時報張迪）

Today, the @ symbol is best known for its role in email addresses. This use began in 1971, when engineer Ray Tomlinson was developing an electronic mail system that could send messages between computers on a network. To make the system viable, he needed a symbol to separate the username from the destination address. Tomlinson chose the @ symbol because it was seldom used in computing at the time, making it less likely to interfere with early computer programs or operating systems. ˇ As soon as he took office, he began a series of reforms in his department. 
χ As soon as he took his office, he began a series of reforms in his department. 
註︰to take office 的 office 不是指辦公室，是抽象名詞，作「職位」解，前面不應有人稱代名詞所有格。 
2. 他們拿起武器保衛城市。 
ˇ They took up arms to defend their city. 
χ They took up their arms to defend their city. 
註︰high 通常指「物」的高大，to take up arms 這一慣用語中不需用人稱代名詞所有格。

χ This is the most beautiful house I have ever set my eyes on.
